subject: SOC 2 findings — management response & remediation timeline for ProspectX
messages:
From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@prospectx.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: SOC 2 exception details and bridge letter

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for sending Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report. Our security team reviewed the report and flagged two exceptions in the "change control" and "logical access" sections related to documented remediation items during the audit period (Q3–Q4 2025). We need a bit more color before we can proceed with procurement:

- Can you provide Redwood's management responses for each exception?
- Do you have evidence of remediation (change logs, deployment tickets, config snapshots) that we can review?
- Will you provide a bridge letter that covers the gap between the report end date and any remediation dates?

If possible, we'd like a short, customer-facing management response plus an internal evidence bundle. Can you also include an expected remediation completion timeline and an owner for each item?

We'd prefer to receive materials by EOD Tuesday (2026-02-17) to keep our procurement window. Happy to set a 30-minute sync if that's easier.

Thanks,
Laura Jensen
Security Lead, ProspectX
laura.jensen@prospectx.com

--
ProspectX - Procurement/Security

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Follow-up: SOC 2 exception details and bridge letter

Rachel — notes below from engineering on the two items called out.

1) Change control exception (audit noted missing evidence for one out-of-window emergency patch):
- Remediation performed: implemented mandatory review step in our CI/CD pipeline for hotfixes (PR gate + test-run guard) on 2025-12-18.
- Owner: Dev Patel (eng services)
- Evidence available: PR #5721 (link in drive), CI pipeline run logs from 2025-12-18, deployment ticket TKT-9882.
- Status: remediation completed and validated via 2 smoke tests and one rollback test.

2) Logical access exception (audit found temporary elevated access for two support engineers without recorded approvals):
- Remediation performed: revoked all temporary elevated roles, enforced time-bound RBAC tokens, and added approval workflows in our identity provider (IdP) on 2026-01-07.
- Owner: Dev Patel (with Security Ops)
- Evidence available: IdP approval logs, audit trail export (CSV), support request TKT-10110, and a screenshot of the updated role policy.
- Status: remediation completed; periodic audit task scheduled monthly to verify token expirations.

I can package the artifacts into remediation-evidence-20260218.zip (sensitive items redacted) and place them in the shared drive. Estimated contents: PR diffs, pipeline logs, ticket exports, IdP audit CSV.

If you want a short technical summary for the customer-facing doc, see the bullet points above. Let me know if you want me on the customer call.

— Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: customer-facing management response & proposed bridge letter text

Hi all — attaching a draft that I propose we send to ProspectX. Short version below — please suggest edits.

DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE (2–3 paragraphs):
Hi Laura / ProspectX team,

Thank you for reviewing our SOC 2 Type II report and for surfacing the exceptions. Redwood takes audit findings seriously. For each exception identified in the audit period, we have implemented corrective actions and validated those changes through testing and audit-log exports. Specifically, we strengthened our change-control process for emergency fixes and enforced time-bound RBAC controls in our identity provider to prevent unapproved access.

We have attached a management response that summarizes the root cause, corrective actions, and owners, along with an evidence bundle for your review. We will provide a bridge letter that covers the remediation steps completed since the report end date and confirm our controls remain effective. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call to walk through the artifacts.

Proposed Bridge Letter (one-paragraph summary):
This letter confirms that Redwood Inference identified two exceptions during the SOC 2 Type II audit period and that both exceptions were remediated after the audit period. The remediation actions are described in the attached management response and evidence package. Redwood confirms that the described remediations are in place as of 2026-02-18 and are subject to ongoing monitoring.

If everyone signs off I will send this to ProspectX on Wed 18 Feb.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
